external.padUsdcNote: The LAUNCHPAD's own testnet USDC (factory/inj1tf79.../USDC, 6dp) and NOT external.usdc, which is the Circle FiatToken. It is quote asset 2 on the pad core, launches 13 graduated against it, and it is a registered quote route on the sink. Two different tokens both reporting symbol() == 'USDC' is a known trap in this deployment.

choice.launchFeeCrankerNote: 1.0.0, deployed 2026-09-06. Plan A6: ONE permissionless call that takes a graduated launch's accrued LP fees all the way to a destroyed burn token. Trading a graduated pool accrues fees inside the locked position and nothing else happens; turning them into a burn was THREE calls - PositionLocker.collect(launchId), claim(currency, launchpadTreasury) once per currency, then the sink's own leg - all permissionless by design and named to nobody. crank(launchId) does all of it; crankMany(uint256[]) is the keeper shape and skips whatever fails. It adds NO trust: every destination was already fixed, so a caller chooses only WHEN and pays the gas. It holds nothing, has no owner and no sweep - and therefore no privileged address at all. Every leg is try/catch'ed, because collect reverts NothingToCollect and claim reverts NothingToClaim on a quiet launch and a helper that reverts on those is useless to a keeper looping over launches. 🔑 Leg ORDER is load-bearing: the launch-token leg is driven FIRST because converting ends in a buyback that spends the sink's whole quote balance including what the claim just delivered, so one call turns both currencies into one swap. 🔴 Its SINK is immutable and it calls convert(Currency,uint256), which exists only from sink 1.2.0 - so a sink redeploy is ALWAYS a cranker redeploy. The compiler enforces the ABI half (it holds the concrete BuybackBurnSink type, not an interface copy) and script 10 asserts SINK()/LOCKER() against the address book. ⚠️ Deployed against positionLocker 1.1.0 only. positionLockerLegacy 1.0.0 has no claim at all - it PUSHES on collect - and an instance pointed at it would work through the try, but that is one more deploy, not a branch inside this one. ✅ WALKED 2026-09-06: crank(20) collected 49,999.99 launch tokens of accrued LP fee, claimed the launchpad's 15,000 (30%) to the sink, converted them to 0.0001828882 wINJ, bought 2,612.554905 burn tokens and burnt 2,090.043924 (80.0000%) - one transaction, 0x847354bdb7e62deda3e8fa5e670fcf20cc573bd17607a7cb54aac066d349f954, block 139188677. The creator's 35,000 stayed credited and untouched, and both the sink and the cranker ended at zero. crankMany([19,20,999]) answers [true,true,false]: launch 19 is SAI-paired so its convert leg has no route and is refused rather than routed (D28's open edge), 999 is unregistered.
choice.launchFeeCrankerLegacyNote: 1.1.0 bytecode, deployed 2026-09-07 by plan A9, bound to choice.positionLockerLegacy. IT IS THE SAME CONTRACT as choice.launchFeeCranker - only the LOCKER constructor argument differs - because the cranker's LOCKER is IMMUTABLE and an instance therefore reaches exactly one locker generation's launches. 🔴 That is not a nicety: the 1.0.0 locker holds launches 13-17, THE BURN TOKEN'S OWN LAUNCH AMONG THEM, and for as long as one cranker existed those fees had nothing scheduled to move them while the keeper's auto-crank ran every fifteen minutes against the 1.1.0 locker and reported a healthy pass every time. Nothing was broken and nothing said anything. ⛔ The answer is a SECOND INSTANCE, never a branch: a cranker that sniffed which generation it faced would be the 'five copies of what is current' problem in a new place, and A6's own header rejected it in advance. It costs nothing to avoid - the 1.0.0 locker has no claim() at all (it PUSHES on collect) and the cranker's try around that leg already tolerates a call to a missing selector, which reverts with EMPTY returndata. test_aSecondInstanceAgainstAPushLockerStillBurns now EXECUTES that claim against a locker without the function rather than asserting it. Deployed from script 10 with CRANKER_LOCKER_KEY=choice.positionLockerLegacy, salt CHOICE-V2/LaunchFeeCrankerLegacy/1.1.0; an unrecognised key REVERTS rather than hashing to a fresh salt, which would deploy a third cranker at an address this book never records. ✅ WALKED 2026-09-07: crankMany([13,14,15,16,17]) - tx 0x515941c2a5c2cf266d8482eb17a9d97056eff5a1a709f4b1436405b7c2d3e86a, block 139261992, 3,360,045 gas for five launches - collected 4.146599163298504232 BRN from launch 14 and 433,778,879,135,765 wei of wINJ from launch 15, converted the launchpad's 30% of the BRN to 79,300,407,425 wei (which PARKED below minBuybackAmount on its own), and then launch 15's collect carried the total over the floor: ONE BoughtBack of 130,212,964,148,155 wei - EXACTLY 30% of launch 15's fee plus launch 14's conversion output, two launches meeting in one swap - bought 1,859.561521822423539087 burn tokens and BURNT 1,487.649217457938831269 (8000 bps, the immutable floor). Supply 998,013,311.328647748425140814 -> 998,011,823.679430290486309545, matching the multicall simulation TO THE WEI. 🔑 Every Cranked event carries claimed0=claimed1=0, which is the push locker's signature: collect had already delivered the money and claim reverted into the try. 🔴 A sink redeploy is a redeploy of BOTH crankers, and the keeper's CRANK_CRANKER must list BOTH - it is a SET since A9, the way PHASE3_SETTLER already was.
choice.clFeeControllerNote: 1.1.0, deployed 2026-09-06, REPLACING 0x36ab137ac1647c16646CA851c2715FBb60f4FD3C. Carries zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee (plan A0, tokenomics D30/D31): a launchpad graduate pays Choice NO protocol fee, so protocolFeesAccrued holds only Choice's own revenue by construction. launchPoolGuardHook is set to choice.launchPoolGuardHook; while it is unset every graduation reverts. Owner = timelock. ⚠️ It ships PARKED - treasuryBps 10000, burnSink = directTransferBurnSink - and it is NEVER pointed at the launchpad's buybackBurnSink. The controller it replaces WAS (treasuryBps 2000 -> that sink), which was the pre-D30 walk configuration and is exactly the link D30 forbids. So Choice's own protocol fee no longer feeds the launchpad's buyback on testnet either; the launchpad's revenue reaches its sink only through launchpad.treasury and PositionLocker.launchpadTreasury. The superseded controller is left in place, timelock-owned, holding nothing, with nothing pointing at it.
choice.infinitySettlerNote: 1.2.0, deployed 2026-09-06, superseding 1.1.0 0x8C4f5418Ff1fb1eA80fA0c5b1e1c4604a7bdfA2d (same code, wrong locker) and 1.0.0 0xC3ED6d3f97D85B243108446a17ed53d896331ac9. Plan A0: lpFee 10000 (the WHOLE 1.00% tier, not the 6722 that composited to 1% alongside a protocol fee) and settle() calls clFeeController.zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee, so a graduate never charges Choice's protocol fee for even one block. The trader pays the same 1%: 9,999 pips before, 10,000 after. Owner = timelock. 🔴 1.1.0 is DEAD - its immutable LOCKER is the 1.0.0 locker, whose register() takes FOUR arguments (pre-contracts-2cf25cc) and therefore has no selector for the five-argument one this repo compiles. Every graduation through it reverted with EMPTY returndata after passing every gate and canary; launch #18 is wedged in CurveFilled because it snapshotted 1.1.0. Script 05 now proves the locker's ABI before it wires anything - see _requireLockerSpeaksOurAbi.
choice.positionLockerNote: 1.1.0, deployed 2026-09-06, REPLACING 0x9b28F31B8AB8ED488B4E8bc7cb432ceaFe60E3Fe. Plan A3, forced early by A0: the PULL version - collect() credits and claim() pays, so one blocked recipient cannot freeze the other side's fees - and register() binds the position to its PoolKey. That fifth argument changes the SELECTOR, which is why the 1.0.0 locker cannot serve any settler built from main. Born owned by the timelock and already pointing at settler 1.2.0. ⚠️ The 1.0.0 locker stays live and holds the positions of launches 13-17; their creator and launchpad fees are still collectable there, through its own push-payment collect(). Nothing new registers into it. 🔑 BOTH lockers' launchpadTreasury point at choice.buybackBurnSink as of 2026-09-06 - that field IS the launchpad revenue feed D30 names, and until A4 it pointed nowhere useful: 1.1.0 at the pad treasury and 1.0.0 at the twice-superseded sink 0xe0248Ebc. 1.1.0 CREDITS the sink (pull) so someone must call claim(currency, sink) and then the sink's own burn/convert/buyback; 1.0.0 PUSHES on collect(). Credits already owed to the previous recipient stay claimable by it - owed is keyed by recipient, so moving this field cannot take or strand them. 🔑 As of 2026-09-07 BOTH now point at the 1.3.0 sink 0x4435DD1a7f61FEfFc00d9283855c9Cc42D29c96D (they pointed at the 1.2.0 sink 0xd8aDFa9E13d9116914837A381392EE2EEf595d4B from 2026-09-06 until A8 redeployed it). 🔴 A SINK REDEPLOY IS ALWAYS A B6 REPOINT OF BOTH LOCKERS, and it is easy to forget: a cranker whose feedIsWired() is false still collects and still claims, it just pays somewhere that does not burn, and BOTH are in that sink's locker set (plan A5) - the 1.0.0 locker stopped being merely historical the moment a launch id became the way the sink finds a pool, because it is the only thing that knows where launches 13-17 graduated. choice.launchFeeCranker (plan A6) collects from the 1.1.0 locker in one call.
choice.buybackBurnSinkNote: 🔴 THIS NOTE DESCRIBES 1.2.0; THE ADDRESS BESIDE IT IS 1.3.0. `buybackBurnSink` was moved to **1.3.0 `0x4435DD1a7f61FEfFc00d9283855c9Cc42D29c96D`** by plan A8 on 2026-09-07 (the second leg: `convert` may now be two legs, the launch's own graduation pool then an owner-REGISTERED pool from the pair asset to QUOTE, and `conversionRoute(currency, launchId)` is what reports it). 1.2.0 was `0xd8aDFa9E13d9116914837A381392EE2EEf595d4B`. Everything below still describes A5 correctly and is kept because 1.3.0 inherits all of it — only the version line and the address were stale. Found 2026-09-07 auditing the deployed stack against the record. --- ORIGINAL 1.2.0 NOTE FOLLOWS --- 1.2.0 TEST deployment, 2026-09-06, REPLACING 1.1.0 0xcC707724b5B91b17ef398E11257E1a61b10bdF20. Plan A5: the sink ASKS a launch's locked position for its real PoolKey instead of DERIVING one from a stored tier. setConversionTier and the conversionTier struct are GONE - that field was a copy of mutable settler config, the fifth such copy after the keeper's PHASE3_SETTLER, the pad backend's CHOICE_V2_SETTLERS, the pad frontend's ADDRESSES.infinitySettlers and script/tools/verify-all.sh, and all four of the others were found stale on the same day. In its place: setLockers(address[]), the position lockers a conversion may read a graduate's pool out of, plus an immutable POSITION_MANAGER the constructor now takes and setLockers checks every candidate against. convert is now convert(Currency,uint256 launchId): the launch id is a HINT, verified not trusted - the key it resolves to must trade exactly {currency, QUOTE} or the call reverts LaunchDoesNotTrade, so no launch id routes a swap through a pool the caller chose. ⚠️ burn(Currency,uint256) can no longer convert a launch token - it carries no launch id - and parks it with the new reason 6, PARK_NEEDS_HINT. That costs nothing under D30, where no ChoiceFeeController points here and launch-token revenue arrives as a bare transfer from PositionLocker.claim; launchFeeCranker is what moves it on. Deployed by CREATE3 from script/09_DeployBuybackBurnSink.s.sol, salt CHOICE-V2/BuybackBurnSink/1.2.0, born timelock-owned. Burn token is the TEST launchpad.burnToken, quote wINJ. MIN_BURN_BPS 8000 (immutable), burnBps 8000. lockers = [positionLocker 1.1.0, positionLockerLegacy 1.0.0], so ONE sink serves both generations - the two answer getPosition and POSITION_MANAGER identically, only register differs. buybackPool was set from the key launchPool(15) returns, which is byte-identical to the one 1.1.0 carried: the derivation was checked against the hand-configured value before it replaced it. ⚠️ TEST guards - minBuybackInterval 60s, maxImpactBps 500, and minBuybackAmount 1e12 rather than 1.1.0's 1e15, lowered because a testnet graduate's accrued LP fee is TENS OF MICRO-wINJ and 1e15 gates every real crank. See the launchpad's own tokenomics before mainnet and do NOT copy any of them there. ✅ WALKED 2026-09-06, BOTH halves of A5 on one sink with NO tier configured anywhere: launch 14's BRN, which graduated on a 6722 pool and is held by the 1.0.0 locker, converted 618.895398 BRN to 0.0000394530 wINJ, bought 1,712.132062 burn tokens and burnt 1,369.705650 of them (80.0000%) - the exact case that was NOT derivable under 1.1.0's installed 10000 tier and whose revenue parked. Launch 20, on a 10000 pool in the 1.1.0 locker, resolves through the same sink in the same block. tx 0xdbb1cbbb98cd36323a5883133e528bcdb9c5d005634246635703ada96b56526a, block 139188471. ⛔ As under D30, no ChoiceFeeController points here - the sink is fed by the pad, through launchpad.treasury and PositionLocker.launchpadTreasury on BOTH lockers. The superseded 1.1.0 and 1.0.0 sinks are left in place, timelock-owned, holding nothing.

launchpad.burnTokenNote: The TEST burn token the buybackBurnSink destroys - launch 15 on this pad, wINJ-paired, graduated under settler 1.0.0 and therefore living on a 6722-pip pool rather than the 10000 A0 installed. It is a launch token like any other; nothing about it is special except that the sink's BURN_TOKEN is immutable and points at it. Mainnet's burn token is a different token and a different sink.

pools.what: The SECOND LEG (plan A2): how a SAI-paired graduate's revenue reaches the sink's QUOTE. Registered with setQuoteRoute, NOT derived - an ordinary pool carries no guard hook, so anyone could open one at the key a formula would name, at any price they chose.
pools.oneSided: wINJ only, ticks 23030-46050. The sink only ever SELLS SAI into this pool, so the only side it needs is the one that BUYS - which is why it could be opened by somebody holding no SAI at all.
pools.warning: The price is an ASSUMPTION, not a market: nothing on chain said what SAI is worth in wINJ, because no pool existed. On mainnet a route must come from a real market, or the quote asset should not be accepted at all.

pools.what: The SECOND LEG for the pad's own USDC (plan A2/A8). Registered with setQuoteRoute. Launch 13 graduated against this asset, so with the route installed its token resolves to TWO legs - across a LOCKER GENERATION, since launch 13 sits in positionLockerLegacy.
pools.poolIdNote: PROVEN by hash, not copied: poolId == keccak256(abi.encode(key)), and getSlot0 at it answers a live pool. That is the strongest form of the rule - the chain's own id is the witness that every field of the key above is right.
pools.seedTickNote: 🔴 NEGATIVE, and that is decimals not price. A pool's price is a ratio of RAW units, so ten of a 6-decimal asset per wINJ is tick -253300 where ten of an 18-decimal one is +23030. Same price, opposite sign.
pools.warning: The price is an ASSUMPTION, not a market - no wINJ/padUSDC pool existed. Same caveat as the SAI route.

meta.forkPinsNote:
✅ CLOSED 2026-09-07, and the way it closed is the lesson. This note used to say the periphery pin was DELIBERATELY AHEAD of this network's deployed bytecode and that redeploying the UniversalRouter from it would close the gap. The first half was true. THE SECOND HALF WAS WRONG, and it cost a deploy to find out.

🔴 THE UNIVERSAL ROUTER DOES NOT COMPILE AGAINST THIS PIN. infinity-universal-router carries its OWN lib/infinity-periphery submodule, and its remappings.txt resolves `infinity-periphery/=lib/infinity-periphery/` to that copy - so when the deploy script is run from that repo, which is the only way the router has ever been deployed, CLRouterBase comes from THERE and not from anything this file names. It was pinned at 481650d, dated 2025-02-05, and upstream's own router main pins the same commit. A third copy of 'which periphery is current', tracked by nothing.

PROVEN AT COST: salt 1.1.0 was deployed on 2026-09-07 to 0xdfa954e35851D71c3c6a4D6c35ACF957bE4CE88f expressly to take the fix, and came out BYTE-IDENTICAL to the router it replaced - both codehash 0x8b9d173ff2516195f39d11fb694ca8a38cd20ec585e149f9122a655c7e738243. That instance is ABANDONED: unowned (owner() is the CREATE3 proxy child), unreferenced, and it must never be adopted. Salt 1.1.0 is burnt.

✅ FIXED by pinning the ROUTER's own periphery submodule to this same 0a2aee8 (infinity-universal-router PR #4), so the whole stack now has ONE periphery and this file names it once. Salt 1.2.0 then produced genuinely different code - 23,358 bytes, codehash 0xf23ccae4573075d84d0a40d4e41d2d37beb0177ae9155780328f4fa50ff368fa - deployed to infinity.universalRouter, owner transferred to the timelock through the Safe. The superseded 1.0.0 router 0x4c7d611F09FB896cd3517cA92CcE6B5d2808DfE7 is left in place, timelock-owned, with nothing pointing at it.

⚠️ AND THE BUMP WAS NOT ONE FIX. 481650d to 0a2aee8 is 19 months and five src/ commits: 9b026be exact-output partial fills, 8261f8d bin add-liquidity slippage check, f39aef4 remove the migrator, 04585d1 position manager helper, and 4452b48 HEXENS AUDIT FEEDBACK. The router had been compiling a periphery that PREDATES THE HEXENS AUDIT RESPONSE while this repo built the quoters and position managers from a post-audit one - two peripheries in one deployment, and the 'src/ is byte-identical to audited upstream' property did not hold for that half. Bumping was the safer option, not the riskier one.

🔑 THE GENERAL RULE, because this will recur: WHICH SUBMODULE A CONTRACT COMPILES AGAINST DEPENDS ON WHICH REPO YOU BUILD IT FROM. Every repo has its own remappings.txt and its own nested copies. The UniversalRouter is the ONLY contract in this deployment built from a fork rather than from contracts/, which is exactly why it alone was stale. Before trusting any pin in this file, check the build root.

✅ 2026-09-07, SECOND PASS — EVERY NESTED COPY NOW AGREES. The pins above name three repos; each of those repos carries its own copies of the others, and those are what a build from THAT repo resolves. All of them were brought into line and MEASURED rather than assumed: infinity-periphery's own lib/infinity-core moved 397723e1 (2025-02-14) -> c53aef3, the core this deployment runs, and infinity-universal-router followed the periphery. Every infinity-core in the tree is now c53aef3 and every infinity-periphery is 78c4e294 - `git submodule status --recursive` is the check. ⚠️ Neither move changed any deployed bytecode: CLPositionManager and CLQuoter are byte-identical across the bump, and so is the UniversalRouter's creation code (0x5e79866f...), because the two core commits in the gap touch pool internals the periphery and router never inline. Nothing needs redeploying. 🔴 What it DID fix is test fidelity: the periphery's 496-test suite had been running against a different core than production.

addressAliases.choice.treasury: the Safe: protocol revenue lands where the signers can move it without waiting out a timelock delay

launchpad.core: The launchpad's LaunchpadCore on 1439, deployed 2026-08-24. Not ours; the pad admin owns it and only the pad admin can setSeederFactory.
launchpad.treasury: the launchpad's FeeTreasury: PositionLocker sends the non-creator share of graduated LP fees here
launchpad.phase3Settler: the CW graduation path this one replaces, kept for reference

addressAliases.choice.infinitySettler: M4 graduation adapter. The launchpad core's seederFactory since 2026-09-05: LaunchpadCore.triggerGraduation transfers both legs here and calls settle, which initialises the CL pool at realPair/poolTokenAmount, mints one full-range position to positionLocker and calls onSettled - all in that one transaction.
addressAliases.choice.launchFeeCranker: Plan A6. crank(launchId) is one permissionless call: PositionLocker.collect, claim per currency to launchpadTreasury, then the sink's own leg for each - which was three transactions nobody was named to send. It holds nothing, owns nothing and can only move money along paths that were already fixed, so the only thing a caller chooses is WHEN. crankMany(uint256[]) is the keeper shape.
addressAliases.choice.positionLockerLegacy: The 1.0.0 PUSH locker, superseded by choice.positionLocker but NOT retired: it holds the positions of launches 13-17, and since plan A5 the sink resolves a launch id through its lockers, so it is the only thing that knows where those launches graduated. It is in buybackBurnSink.lockers() for exactly that reason. Its collect() pays out directly rather than crediting, and it has no claim().
addressAliases.choice.positionLocker: Permanent home for every graduated launch's seed position. collect(launchId) is permissionless and splits the LP fees creator / launchpad.treasury by the launch's own creatorFeeShareBps; nothing in it can move the liquidity or the NFT.
addressAliases.choice.launchPoolGuardHook: beforeInitialize ONLY (bitmap 1), so it is consulted once in a pool's life and can never tax, block or freeze a swap. It permissions graduation-pool creation to the settler (D15), which is why every graduation pool is keyed to it forever.
addressAliases.choice.choiceRouter: M5.4 cross-vault router: one end-to-end minimumReceive across TWO Infinity deployments. Only Choice's vault exists on 1439, so execute() reverts NotCrossVault here by design - single-deployment routes go straight to the universalRouter. A second vault is added with setVault from the timelock.
addressAliases.pools: The bin entry carries binStep where the CL ones carry tickSpacing. Both pack at offset 16 of `parameters`, so the words are identical for the same number and only `poolType` tells them apart here - as on chain, where only PoolKey.poolManager does.

firstGraduation.note: The first launch to graduate onto Choice v2, walked end to end on testnet 2026-09-05. Recorded because the poolId and tokenId are the only durable handles on it: Injective serves no receipt, so nothing else can be looked up from the transaction hash.
firstGraduation.quoteAssetNote: the launchpad's own testnet USDC (6dp), NOT external.usdc - the pad quotes its own
firstGraduation.graduationGasNote: measured, not estimated: block 139052885 held this transaction alone, so the block's gasUsed IS the transaction's

a5a6Walk.note: Plan A5 and A6 proven on chain, 2026-09-06. A5: one sink, NO conversion tier configured anywhere, resolving two DIFFERENT fee tiers held in two DIFFERENT locker generations. A6: one call from accrued LP fees to destroyed supply. Recorded here because Injective testnet serves no receipt by hash - the block numbers are the durable handles.

a5.claim: a launch that graduated on an EARLIER fee tier converts and burns, which is precisely what the derived tier could not do - launch 14 sat on a 6722 pool while conversionTier held 10000, so its revenue parked with nothing to look at
a5.feedStep: collect(14) on the 1.0.0 locker pushed 618.895398 BRN and 0.0000804 wINJ to the sink - 30% of the accrued fee, the launchpad's share
a5.proven: Converted(618.895398 BRN -> 0.0000394530 wINJ), BoughtBack(0.0001198530 wINJ -> 1,712.132062 burn tokens), Burnt(1,369.705650 / 342.426412) = 80.0000%. The quote OFFERED exceeds the quote CONVERTED because the collect's own wINJ leg was still sitting in the sink: both halves of one LP fee met in a single buyback.
a5.sameSinkOtherTier: launchPool(20) on the same sink answers a 10000-pip pool held by the 1.1.0 locker, in the same block. Two tiers, two lockers, one sink, zero configuration.

a6.claim: one permissionless call takes a graduated launch from accrued LP fees to a burnt token
a6.proven: Cranked(20): collected 49,999.999999 launch tokens, claimed the launchpad's 15,000 (30%) to the sink, Converted(15,000 -> 0.0001828882 wINJ), BoughtBack(-> 2,612.554905 burn tokens), Burnt(2,090.043924 / 522.510981) = 80.0000%. The wINJ leg was driven second and parked with nothing left to buy with, which is the leg ORDER working: convert first, and its output plus the claimed quote are one buyback.
a6.creatorUntouched: the creator's 35,000 tokens stayed credited in the locker and were neither paid nor taken
a6.endState: sink and cranker both at zero in every currency
a6.batch: crankMany([19,20,999]) answers [true,true,false] - 19 is SAI-paired so its convert leg is refused (D28's open edge), 999 is unregistered

a4Graduation.note: Plan A4 proven on the tier mainnet will actually use. Launch 20 was created for this: wINJ-paired, micro curve (targetMulBps 2000, so a 3 wINJ raise rather than the standard 15), graduated through settler 1.2.0 onto a 10000-pip pool, and BuybackBurnSink 1.1.0 converted its token to wINJ against that pool and burnt the tokens it bought. Recorded because Injective testnet serves no receipt by hash, so the poolId is the only durable handle.
a4Graduation.padRowIdNote: the pad api keys /launches/{id} on the DB ROW id, not the on-chain launchId - two id namespaces, and reading the wrong one answers about a different launch entirely
a4Graduation.derivationProven: BuybackBurnSink.conversionPool(launchToken) returns exactly this key - the sink is never told a launch's pool, it derives it from conversionTier plus the two currencies, and the guard hook is what makes a derived key trustworthy
a4Graduation.burnProven: burn(launchToken, 5e24) emitted Converted(5,000,000 token -> 0.0623 wINJ), BoughtBack(0.0624 wINJ -> 894,357.92 burn tokens) and Burnt(715,486.33 / 178,871.58) - 80.0000%, the immutable floor. The quote offered exceeds the quote converted because the sink still held 0.0000999 wINJ from an earlier PositionLocker collect, so the accrued LP fee was spent in the same buyback.
a4Graduation.currencyOrderNote: currency0 is the QUOTE and currency1 the launch token, because 0x0000000088 < 0xA2975e3c

a0Graduation.note: Plan A0 / tokenomics D30+D31 proven on chain: the FIRST launch to graduate paying Choice no protocol fee. Recorded because Injective testnet serves no receipt by hash, so the poolId is the only durable handle. Read getSlot0(poolId) on infinity.clPoolManager: protocolFee 0, lpFee 10000. The wall was checked both ways in the same session - the wINJ/USDT pool below still reads protocolFee 671908 (164 per direction) and zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee reverts NotALaunchPool on it.
a0Graduation.quoteAssetNote: the pad's testnet SAI, 18dp - the launch token is the EVM-only issuance lane (denom erc20:0xb654...), so no Cosmos message was involved in creating it
a0Graduation.compositeSwapFeeNote: calculateSwapFee(0, 10000) = 10000, exactly the 1.00% tier. The pre-A0 split charged calculateSwapFee(3299, 6722) = 9,999 - one pip in a million less, so A0 is trader-neutral to within that pip.
a0Graduation.permissionlessRepairProven: zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee on this key, called from 0x...dEaD, succeeds and changes nothing - the function is permissionless and idempotent
a0Graduation.currencyOrderNote: currency0 is the QUOTE here and currency1 the launch token, because 0x7E6f < 0xb654 - the settler sorts by address, so which leg is currency0 differs per launch. Derivable from the two addresses above; not repeated as its own field, because a value that appears under two keys is exactly what the address book's duplicate check exists to catch.
